deviations.description: Extend test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh with the plan's literal fixture shapes: two tasks sharing an identical path, and a directory entry covering a sibling's file
deviations.reason: Discovered empirically (an earlier draft used exactly those two fixture shapes) that orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's pre-existing in_batch file_scope collision check (lib/file-scope-overlap.sh's scopes_overlap_first: exact-string match OR either side a literal directory-prefix of the other) already, unconditionally, defers one of any two same-cycle candidates whose declared file_scope entries are identical or in a true directory/ancestor relationship -- with no override for in_batch pairs (--allow-scope-collision only lifts a cross_batch collision). Those two fixture shapes are therefore structurally unreachable live through the integration path (run_sut). Adapted Cases A/B to the REAL reachable gap this producer closes instead: a glob entry is documented as "invisible to the symmetric Overlap predicate ... by design" (is_glob_entry's own comment), so a glob-vs-concrete-path pair sails through admission un-deferred even though it genuinely contends -- this is exactly Option 3(ii)'s value-add beyond the pre-existing admission gate. Added a standalone Case G (Group 27's function-extraction precedent) to unit-test the directory-containment branch of _paths_contend directly, proving it correct on its own terms even though live traffic never reaches it through this particular integration path. All six scenarios named in the plan's task list are covered; only the CONCRETE fixture shapes for two of them changed.
